On the 1938 map, Oman (British Raj) is the Sultanate of Muscat and Oman under Sultan Said bin Taimur, who ruled from 1932 to 1970 in close tie with British India.

Oman had once been a sea power with lands in East Africa, but in 1861 it split from the Sultanate of Zanzibar and grew poor. Britain kept a political agent in Muscat, and the sultan's money and foreign affairs ran through British hands. Inland, the tribes of the interior followed an elected imam. The Treaty of Seeb of 1920 left the interior to the Imamate of Oman while the sultan held the coast.

Said bin Taimur kept the country closed and poor, with few schools or roads. His son Qaboos overthrew him in 1970 and spent the new oil money on rapid change. See also Muscat and Oman for the earlier map years.
sum: On the 1938 map, Oman (British Raj) is the Sultanate of Muscat and Oman under Sultan Said bin Taimur, who ruled from 1932 to 1970 in close tie with British India.
